disambiguation.heading: 12. The semantic strike is not the strike of the semantic proletariat
disambiguation.text:
## 12. The semantic strike is not the strike of the semantic proletariat

The Semantic Strike (#1427) does not mean the proletariat withholds semantic labor. The strike does not stop production; it withholds one inference: **institutional selection ⇏ truth about existence or value.** Its operating rule is provenance preservation: preserve where permitted, choose where free, disclose where constrained, refuse where compelled. Semantic class struggle is broader than the Semantic Strike; the strike is one cross-substrate refusal within the larger struggle over semantic technique.

---

captures.description: A BARE CONCEPT PHRASE RESOLVES TO THE ARCHIVE'S DEFINITION, AND THE ARCHIVE'S NEGATION IS THE COMPOSITION'S FIRST MOVE. Issued unquoted, incognito and logged out, 'semantic proletariat' returns a definition built from the archive's own Medium piece of 25 August: a class position occupied by workers who produce and circulate meaning but do not own or control the semantic means of production. The composition then structures its Core Definition in three bullets, and the FIRST is the archive's exclusion, carried whole -- 'Not a demographic: It is not an income bracket, a job title, an identity group, or a simple synonym for content creators.' That is the cited piece's title thesis promoted to the lede of the definition, which means the archive's characteristic form, definition by what the thing is not, survived composition as structure rather than as a sentence. Wikipedia's 'Proletariat' is present as a source card and governs nothing in the body: the generic entity that owns the root term supplied the industrial analogy at most, while the specialisation supplied the definition. The author does not appear in the composition -- Lee Sharks is legible only on the source card -- which is the same erasure the 'semantic economy' capture recorded two days earlier at four citations. Twenty-five days from publication to concept-level composition governance at an unprimed address.
